question: Is the GaSe4 tetrahedron regular? Give the Ga–Se bond length and the Se–Ga–Se angle distribution.

source.lines: frames 190 (the question and the steps), 254 (the answer's start) and 238 (its end and the Outcome chip), counted from 0
source.note: the README's Copilot GIF (PR #66); transcribed from the rendered answer: list items written as "- ", the inline code as `…`, digit-group spaces as plain spaces, and the Outcome line rebuilt from its chip ("Achieved" and the note as shown) in the prompt's "Outcome: <status> — <note>" form

text:
The GaSe₄ polyhedron is built from the Ga–Se first coordination shell.

- Window chosen: the whole first shell from `find_gr_peaks` for Ga–Se, 2.18–2.79 Å. This is the first-shell window (onset to first deep minimum) and it contains the single peak at 2.42 Å (FWHM 0.21 Å). The 2.2 Å closest-approach constraint cuts the distribution: g(r) just above it is 9 % of the first peak, so Ga–Se pairs pile up against the constraint — it is constraint-limited; the constraint, not the data, shapes the low-r side of the peak.
- Coordination: mean 3.99 Se per Ga in 2.18–2.79 Å, with 3 948 of 4 000 Ga atoms having 4 neighbours and 51 having 3. That is the ideal tetrahedral coordination.
- Bond length: Ga–Se mean 2.434 Å, sd 0.095 Å in the 2.18–2.79 Å window.
- Se–Ga–Se angles: 23 842 angles around 4 000 Ga atoms, mean 109.4°, sd 4.1°. Mode 109.5° with share 0.94. The sin θ-corrected 10° histogram peaks at 100–110° (6.7) and 110–120° (5.3), with essentially no weight outside ~90–130°. Within 15° of 109.5° the share is 1.

The angle distribution is centred on the ideal tetrahedral angle 109.5° with a modest spread, and the coordination is essentially four. The polyhedron is effectively regular within the sampling of this run.

Outcome: achieved — the GaSe₄ tetrahedron is essentially regular with Ga–Se 2.434 Å ± 0.095 Å and Se–Ga–Se centred at 109.4° ± 4.1°.
